notes.claim: Instantaneous electrical current is the time derivative of the charge that flows, written i = dq/dt.
An ampere is one coulomb of charge per second, which is the unit of this rate.
Differentiating a position function at a given time gives the velocity at that time.
The current through a capacitor equals the capacitance times the rate of change of its voltage.
The MCA syllabus asks for velocity from displacement-time functions; the HN unit asks for the rate of change of a variable in an engineering problem.
Capacitance is charge per volt: one farad holds one coulomb for each volt across the plates (C = Q/V, so q = Cv). Added for i5 (review fix).
The voltage across an inductor is the derivative of the current through it, multiplied by its inductance in henrys (v = L di/dt). Added for i5 (review fix).
As a capacitor-style charge builds up to its maximum, its derivative, the current, decreases towards zero. Added for i5 (review fix: the charging sketch).
